lines.text: Risk factors for developing osteoporosis include which of the following?
The answer is low calcium intake.
This thin, porous bone looks very sad. It is osteoporosis.
Next to it stands an empty glass. That is low calcium intake.
A high dietary calcium intake promotes calcium absorption and suppresses PTH release and bone dissolution, so it protects bone.
Excess alcohol, a sedentary lifestyle, early menopause, and a thin body habitus also promote bone loss.
Remember: low calcium intake is a risk factor for osteoporosis.
Which statement about haemophilia A is true?
The answer: it affects the intrinsic, rather than the extrinsic, pathway of coagulation.
This boy has bruises, and they come easily, even after small knocks.
The intrinsic road is blocked, and one brick is missing.
The missing brick is clotting factor eight, a member of the intrinsic pathway.
Haemophilia A is X-linked recessive, so it primarily affects males. Female carriers usually do not bleed.
There is a tendency toward easy bruising and haemorrhage after trauma or operations.
Remember: haemophilia A affects the intrinsic pathway.
A thirty-six-year-old man has a neck tumour. It has damaged his left cervical sympathetic chain ganglion. Which of the following physical signs would you expect?
The answer is ptosis on the left.
This thirty-six-year-old man has a neck tumour on the left side.
The tumour has damaged the left cervical sympathetic chain, shown by the spark.
And look at his left eye. The lid droops. That is ptosis on the left.
The pupil is constricted. That is miosis.
This is Horner's syndrome. Loss of sympathetic supply also gives anhidrosis, facial flushing, and enophthalmos.
Lateral deviation of the eye would suggest damage to the third cranial nerve instead.
Remember: sympathetic chain damage gives ptosis and a small pupil on the same side.
